[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Mastering MultiIndex (Hierarchical Indexing) in Pandas"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Hierarchical indexing, or MultiIndex, is a powerful feature in Pandas that allows you to store and manipulate panel data with multiple dimensions using standard two-dimensional DataFrames. This tutorial covers the creation, selection, and manipulation of MultiIndex structures."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Creating a MultiIndex DataFrame"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"There are several ways to construct a MultiIndex. You can pass a list of lists to the index parameter, use pandas.MultiIndex.from_tuples, or use pandas.MultiIndex.from_product. Here is an example using from_product:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Define levels
years = [2022, 2023]
quarters = ['Q1', 'Q2']

# Create a MultiIndex
index = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([years, quarters], names=['Year', 'Quarter'])

# Create DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({'Revenue': [100, 120, 130, 140], 'Cost': [80, 90, 95, 100]}, index=index)
print(df)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Data Slicing and Selection"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Accessing data in a MultiIndex DataFrame requires understanding how levels are nested. You can use standard .loc[] indexing by passing tuples representing the hierarchical levels."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Select data for a specific year and quarter
print(df.loc[(2023, 'Q1')])

# Select data for a specific outer index (all quarters in 2022)
print(df.loc[2022])"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To select data across inner levels while keeping outer levels, the slice(None) object is extremely useful."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"# Select 'Q1' across all years
print(df.loc[(slice(None), 'Q1'), :])"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Swapping and Stacking Levels"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pandas provides intuitive methods to reorganize your hierarchical indices. The swaplevel() function exchanges two levels, while stack() and unstack() move data between columns and rows."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"# Swap the Year and Quarter levels
df_swapped = df.swaplevel('Year', 'Quarter')
print(df_swapped)

# Unstack the inner index to pivot it into columns
df_unstacked = df.unstack(level='Quarter')
print(df_unstacked)"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Aggregation by Level"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"When analyzing hierarchical data, you often want to aggregate metrics along a specific level. You can use the groupby() or sum() (with the level parameter) to compute statistics across dimensions."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Calculate the sum across the Year level
print(df.groupby(level='Year').sum())

# Alternatively, use level parameter in aggregation functions
print(df.sum(level='Year'))"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Best Practices"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always sort your MultiIndex using df.sort_index() before slicing to avoid performance warnings and incorrect slices."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Name your index levels using the names parameter for better readability and easier groupby operations."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use pd.IndexSlice with .loc[] to write cleaner multi-level slicing expressions."}]
